7. **Newton's method of approximation to the roots of equations.**

Let ξ be an approximation to a root of an algebraical equation $f(x) = 0$, the actual root being ξ + h. Then

$$
0=f(\xi+h)=f(\xi)+hf'(\xi)+\frac{1}{2}h^{2}f''(\xi+\theta_{2}h),
$$

so that

$$
h=-\frac{f(\xi)}{f'(\xi)}-\frac{1}{2}h^{{}_{2}f}\frac{{}''(\xi+\theta_{2}h)}{f'(\xi)}.
$$

It follows that in general a better approximation than $x = ξ$ is

$$
x=\xi-\frac{f(\xi)}{f'(\xi)}.
$$
